summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis report (P6) proposing that humanin-class mitochondria-derived peptides (HN/HNG) blunt FOXO4-DRI senolytic killing to the same degree as navitoclax, and that FOXO4-DRI kill depends on Bax/Bak MOMP execution. The claim is entirely predictive/theoretical — no experiments have been run. All supporting evidence is drawn from published literature, and the key experimental variables (matched head-to-head blunt comparison, Bax/Bak epistasis) are explicitly labeled UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata and Policy
content_blocks.content: Public report only (PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY). Report date: 2026-09-25. STATUS_LABEL: NEGATIVE. Risk class: research-discussion. Polarity: negative. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Private vault: NONE. Note: Identical science to openlabs.md; no sequence, analog list, or unpublished construct; no mol_ keys.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim (P6)
content_blocks.content: On a matched senescent-culture panel, humanin-class MDP (HN or HNG) blunts FOXO4-DRI senescent-cell clearance as much as it blunts navitoclax — |(%kill_drop_FOXO4-DRI) − (%kill_drop_navitoclax)| ≤ 15 percentage points, with both arms showing a pre-registered ≥20% relative kill drop vs senolytic alone; and FOXO4-DRI kill is lost or strongly reduced under Bax/Bak LOF or BAX-channel block (MOMP-execution gate).

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale and Mechanism
content_blocks.content: P5 hypothesized that FOXO4-DRI's distinct entry point (FOXO4–p53 axis) would spare it from HN antagonism relative to navitoclax (Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w). P6 challenges this: if execution still converges on Bax/Bak MOMP, pathway-sparing fails and HN should equally blunt both senolytics. Mechanism sketch: FOXO4-DRI enters via FOXO4–p53; navitoclax via Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w; HN binds Bax and blocks mitochondrial translocation/cytochrome c release. Endothelial FOXO4-DRI work frames a p53/BCL-2/Caspase-3 cascade — Bcl-2-family nodes can sit downstream of the FOXO4–p53 trigger without proving Bax/Bak necessity or measuring HN co-treatment.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
Four key references underpin the hypothesis:
1. PMID 28340339 (Baar 2017, Cell, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2017.02.031, PMC5556182): FOXO4-DRI perturbs FOXO4–p53 → senescent-cell apoptosis; not Bcl-xL occupancy; no HN arm.
2. PMID 12732850 (Guo 2003, Nature, DOI 10.1038/nature01627): Humanin binds Bax; blocks mitochondrial translocation/cytochrome c release.
3. PMID 26711051 (Zhu 2016, Aging Cell, DOI 10.1111/acel.12445, PMC4854923): Navitoclax senolytic via Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w; cell-type restricted.
4. PMID 41625068 (2025, Front. Bioeng., DOI 10.3389/fbioe.2025.1729166, PMC12852416): Endothelial FOXO4-DRI framed via p53/BCL-2/Caspase-3; not Bax/Bak DKO; no HN co-treatment.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Distinct FOXO4–p53 entry protects FOXO4-DRI from HN MOMP blockade relative to navitoclax (P5 pathway-sparing hope), so equal blunt/Bax epistasis need not be tested.
Baseline measured: All four supporting data points are LITERATURE only. humanin∩FOXO4=0; humanin∩navitoclax∩senolytic=0; matched FOXO4-DRI±HN vs navitoclax±HN + Bax/Bak LOF = UNKNOWN. Equal % blunt (|Δdrop|≤15 pp; each ≥20% relative drop) = PREDICTION. P5 does not already prove this gate.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat P5 as proving P6 — P5 listed shared MOMP as a caveat; it did not measure equal blunt or Bax epistasis.
2. BCL-2 cascade language ≠ Bax requirement — PMID 41625068 is not a Bax/Bak LOF kill of FOXO4-DRI.
3. Equal blunt is stronger than shared MOMP necessity — HN potency may differ by senolytic even if both need Bax/Bak; cell-type mismatch (navitoclax-insensitive SCs) confounds H2H.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Method and Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content:
Method: propose-assay (NOT_RUN). Ablation analysis: (1) Without H2H % blunt, separate LITERATURE legs cannot show HN equal-blunts both senolytics. (2) Equal blunt alone does not establish the MOMP-execution gate; pathway-sparing could fail for other reasons. (3) Treating P5 or 41625068 cascade language as already deciding the gate would invent an epistasis/H2H result left UNKNOWN.
Refutation criteria: On the pre-registered matched panel, HN spares FOXO4-DRI (FOXO4 relative kill drop <20% or outside the equal-blunt band while navitoclax is blunted), or FOXO4-DRI kill survives Bax/Bak LOF/BAX-channel block — pathway-sparing/MOMP-independent execution survives.

key_findings: All experimental variables are either LITERATURE-derived or explicitly labeled UNKNOWN/PREDICTION — no in-house experiments have been run (execution_status=NOT_RUN).
Central claim is a PREDICTION: HN/HNG blunts FOXO4-DRI kill ≥20% relative drop AND |drop_FOXO4 − drop_navitoclax| ≤ 15 percentage points on a matched senescent-culture panel.
FOXO4-DRI entry via FOXO4–p53 axis is established by literature (Baar 2017, PMID 28340339), but Bax/Bak necessity for FOXO4-DRI kill is UNKNOWN.
HN–Bax binding and MOMP block is established by literature (Guo 2003, PMID 12732850), but no HN co-treatment with FOXO4-DRI has been measured.
Navitoclax senolytic activity via Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w is established by literature (Zhu 2016, PMID 26711051); cell-type restriction is a confound for head-to-head comparison.
Endothelial FOXO4-DRI p53/BCL-2/Caspase-3 framing (PMID 41625068) does NOT constitute Bax/Bak epistasis evidence and includes no HN co-treatment.
P5 is explicitly stated to NOT prove P6 — shared MOMP was listed as a caveat in P5, not a measured result.
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; cost tier: 1 (low cost); IP class: momp-execution-gate; no vault hold.
STATUS_LABEL is NEGATIVE — the hypothesis is framed as a negative/challenging result relative to P5's pathway-sparing hope.
Key proposed assay: matched senescent culture panel with FOXO4-DRI ± HN vs navitoclax ± HN, viability + cytochrome-c/MOMP markers, optional Bax/Bak LOF or BAX-channel block.
